faq.a: A hinge joint lets bones move in one direction, back and forth, like a door. Your elbow, knee and finger joints are hinge joints.

faq.q: What is a ball and socket joint?
faq.a: It is a joint where a rounded end of one bone fits into a cup in another. It allows movement in almost every direction, including circles. Your shoulders and hips are ball and socket joints.

faq.q: Which joint lets you shake your head?
faq.a: A pivot joint between the top two bones of your neck. The ring-shaped first bone, the atlas, turns around a peg sticking up from the second bone, the axis.
asks: Tell me about the neck pivot

faq.a: No. Some are fixed, like the sutures that lock the plates of an adult skull together. Others, like those between the bones of the spine, move only a little.
asks: Tell me about the skull sutures

faq.q: Why is the shoulder easier to injure than the hip?
faq.a: The shoulder's socket is shallow, which gives a huge range of movement but less stability. The hip's socket is deep, so it is more stable but moves less.
asks: Why can the shoulder move so much?

facts: An adult human skeleton usually has 206 bones.
The atlas and axis, the top two neck vertebrae, form a pivot joint that lets the head turn.
